title: LLM prefetch + routing roadmap (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: sketch a lightweight, experimental roadmap for a KV-prefetch + routing system that lowers tail latency and token cost for short interactive chat requests while preserving output quality. This is a personal scratchpad - lots of TODOs, open Qs, and rough ideas.

Summary / hypothesis:
- Many live chat requests repeat prefixes (system prompt, few-shot examples, user metadata). If we prefetch KV cache for common prefixes and route requests to nodes that already have warmed caches, we can reduce per-request latency and GPU compute.
- Combine prefetch with routing policies: route low-latency-sensitive requests to high-efficiency nodes and latency-sensitive to nodes with warm KV caches or hot sequences.
- Short-term win: prefetched KV cache + affinity routing for top 5-20 most common prefixes -> measurable p50/p95 latency improvement and token-cost reduction due to fewer re-computations.

Success metrics (proposed):
- p50/p95 latency for interactive chat (<= 200ms p50, reduce p95 by 30% for targeted flows)
- Tokens served per GPU-second (increase by 10-25% for routed traffic)
- Quality regression <= 1% on held-out evals (automated prompt set)
- Error rate / misrouted fallbacks < 0.5%

User stories / personas:
- Product engineer (chat widget): "I need consistent sub-200ms interactive responses for short queries and cost predictability for high QPS."
- Platform engineer: "I want knobs to pin routing policies, TTLs for cache entries, and visibility into cache hits per route."
- Security/compliance: "Prefetch must not leak tenant-specific data; prefetch only allowed for safe prefixes or customer-owned contexts."

Rough feature list (MVP -> v1):
MVP (3-6 weeks experiments):
- Lightweight prefix hashing and top-k prefix detector (server-side telemetry)
- Manual prefetch API: allow ops to prime KV for a prefix on a given pool/instance
- Affinity routing: simple header-based routing to instances with prefetched entries (sticky for short TTL)
- Metrics: cache-hit rate, latency by route, fallback count
- Safety: prefix whitelist, tenant isolation check

v1 (after initial validation, 8-12 weeks):
- Auto-prefetcher: heuristics to prefetch based on frequency + rate of repetition
- Storage for prefetched KV snapshots with TTLs (memory-backed on instance + optional shared cache)
- Smart routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, capacity-aware fallback
- Canary rollout and warm-up tooling in Console
- Eval integration: automated quality checks for prefetched variants

Design notes / implementation ideas:
- Prefetch representation: store KV cache snapshot for the transformer decoder state after tokenizing prefix. Represent as list of KV tensors or serialized cache blob depending on runtime format.
- Warm-up API: POST /v1/prefetch {prefix_hash, model, seq_len, target_pool} -> returns instance ids primed.
- Routing: add route metadata to request: prefix_hash (optional), latency_target (low/medium/high), cost_priority. Router consults ring of instances and selects those with matching prefix and available capacity. If none, fallback to fastest idle instance.
- Eviction: TTL per prefix entry + LRU by memory footprint. Track per-instance memory budget.
- Safety: do not prefetch prefixes that contain PII or customer tokens unless explicitly authorized. Add analyzer that flags prefixes with personal data heuristics.

Experiments (quick experiments to run):
- A/B: enable manual prefetch for top-10 prefixes for 10% traffic -> measure p95 and token usage with control.
- Simulation: replay recent requests (anonymized) against a simulated cluster to estimate hit rates for top-k prefixes and memory requirements.
- Quality test: run eval prompt set for prefetched vs cold-start responses to detect regressions (semantic and token diff).

Open questions / risks:
- Storage format: do we store raw KV tensors (fast) or a compact serialized form (portable across minor runtime versions)?
- Cross-model compatibility: caches are model-version-specific. How to handle model rollouts? Versioned snapshots, + auto-invalidate.
- Cost of maintaining warm instances: tradeoff between warm capacity and idle cost. Need to model economics (cost per warm instance vs savings per token).
- Multi-tenant isolation: ensure cached KV from tenant A never leaks to B. Prefer instance-level isolation and tenant-aware keys.
- Fallback correctness: when routing to a prefetched instance but prefix mismatch occurs (partial match), how to gracefully merge KV (or rebuild).

Risk mitigations:
- Start with single-tenant experiments (internal customer or Redwood-owned traffic) to eliminate cross-tenant risk.
- Conservative whitelist for prefixes allowed in prefetch during MVP.
- Add telemetry to detect semantic divergence quickly and auto-disable prefetch for offending prefix.

Operational / rollout plan (rough):
- Week 0-2: telemetry + top-prefix analysis + simulation code.
- Week 3-6: implement manual prefetch API + affinity routing + basic console metrics. Run internal canary on internal apps.
- Week 7-10: add auto-prefetch heuristics + centralized storage + eviction + richer routing policies. Expand to small external customers.
- Week 11+: full productization: Console controls, safety audits, pricing experiments.

Notes for follow-ups / TODOs:
- TODO: ask eng-serving-runtime about serialization format and whether current runtime can import/export KV blobs (Priya).
- TODO: schedule sync with SRE on instance memory budgeting and eviction policies (Jordan).
- TODO: get a short list of candidate internal apps for canary (Aisha).
- TODO: draft a short Confluence page summarizing experiment plan and metrics (Marta).

Quick sketches / API examples:
- Prefetch request: POST /v1/prefetch?model=redwood-v1&target_pool=low-latency
  body: {"prefix": "<system>...<user>...", "max_seq_len": 128, "ttl_secs": 300} -> response: {"prefetch_id":"pf_123", "instances":["i-12","i-13"]}
- Inference request (optionally include prefix hash): POST /v1/generate
  headers: {"X-Prefix-Hash": "pf_123", "X-Latency-Target": "low"}

Potential quick wins to check first (priority order):
1) Top-20 prefixes analysis and mem footprint estimation (low effort)
2) Manual prefetch + affinity routing prototype on a single small pool (medium effort)
3) Simulated replay to estimate hit rate and cost savings (low -> medium)

References / related notes:
- Related scratchpads: llm-prefetch-kv-cache-scratchpad.json, llm-prefetch-prd-scratchpad-aisha-khan.json
- Past experiments logs: internal/experiments/prefetch-2024 (ask Jordan for link)

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a short PRD + experiment plan once I sync with runtime and SRE.

Marta
